title: 28th Sitting of first Session of 2025
presiding: Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Speaker of the Majlis)
summary: The 28th sitting opened at 09:03 on 7 May 2025. Minutes of the 21 to 24 January sittings were accepted, and the Transport and Civil Aviation Minister answered questions, mostly on the planned MTCC electric taxi line, RTL ferries and airports. Members then continued the debate on the government's new Civil Aviation Bill, which ended for the day without a vote ahead of a 30-minute recess. After the recess the Finance Committee's report on the Customs Service audit reports for 2012 to 2019 was debated and passed 50 to 0.

items.title: Opening of the sitting
items.outcome: Sitting opened at 09:03 with the opening prayer

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: 25 members present, 7 on leave, 2 on official travel at the opening

items.title: Approval of minutes (sittings 21 to 24, 2025)
items.outcome: No amendments filed; chair declared the minutes accepted

items.title: Announcements by the chair: committee membership change
items.outcome: Ibrahim Didi (Kolamaafushi) replaces Ismail Nizar (North Feydhoo) on the Judiciary Committee as a PNC member

items.title: Questions to the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation
items.outcome: Minister answered a question from North Galolhu and follow-ups from 11 other members, mainly on the MTCC electric taxi line

items.title: Unfinished business: debate on the Maldives Civil Aviation Bill (government bill, sponsored by Abdulla Shazeem)
items.outcome: Debated by 8 members; debate closed for the day, to continue at a later sitting; 30-minute recess

items.title: Committee reports: Finance Committee report on Customs Service audit reports 2012 to 2019
Voting on the Finance Committee report

speakers.name: Mohamed Ameen
positions: As Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, said the MTCC electric taxi line will be self-sustaining, with the state aiding only capital investment.
Said about 1,600 taxis are registered in Male but service at needed hours is lacking, and the line adds several vehicle sizes and charging stations.
Said RTL ferries are about 80 percent subsidised and a nationwide RTL roll-out plan is under way.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked the minister to share any analysis behind the claim that the MTCC taxi line will not hurt existing taxi drivers, or explain why.
Asked why the government should enter a business that could be regulated instead.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Asked when an MTCC ferry would serve Isdhoo zone and when RTL services would start in Laamu atoll.
In the bill debate, said easy travel is key to developing atolls and backed a Kadhdhoo international airport and an airport for Isdhoo.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked whether MTCC would need government subsidies, when the Friday RTL ferry in the north returns, and about linking RTL to resorts.
Asked if adding 100 taxis would fix the service shortage, or whether the real problem is taxis or the roads.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked how far Kaadedhdhoo airport development has got, and whether it would be done with the current operator or by the state.
In the bill debate, supported the Civil Aviation Bill and urged better standards at Kaadedhdhoo airport.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the Civil Aviation Bill but argued airports should be built only where studies show an economic return, citing Mathiveri as a good site.
In the audit report debate, said audit reports must be acted on promptly, otherwise the financial system cannot improve.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked whether the minister had tried to reach North Galolhu's member, in writing or by phone, for the basis of his question.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Cited the 10 February 2025 debate and asked whether government taxi policy had changed since PNC members said no taxi line was planned.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Suggested colour-coded taxis, as in other countries, with set numbers licensed for Male and Hulhumale, and asked if this had been tried.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Recalled the President's campaign pledges to stop the garage-city policy and help taxi drivers, and asked how they square with the new line.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked how much work preceded the decision to enter the taxi business, and what is being done about RTL boats and delays.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked why taxi drivers were not told the plain facts, and about RTL speedboats in the southern atolls out of service for months.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked how much money the government will spend on the electric taxi fleet and whether this or fixing parking is the real priority.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked why Fuvahmulah to Male ticket prices have not come down, whether another airline applied for the route, and when the airport will be upgraded.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Welcomed the Civil Aviation Bill to replace the 2001 act, noting it requires an airport master plan and an accident investigation agency.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Said the bill sets up regulation after air-safety incidents and that the government aims for an airport within about 30 minutes of most places.
Raised preparing for the effects of the India-Pakistan conflict, especially food import security.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the bill but said existing domestic airports need repair and services before new ones are promised.
Backed an airport in Noonu atoll for Velidhoo, Holhudhoo and Foddoo, citing earlier unmet promises.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Called the bill important for an island nation and spoke up for Hulhudhoo and Meedhoo, where sea travel is hard in rough weather.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Welcomed the bill but raised concern that policy-making power rests only with the minister, and questioned the cost-benefit of many airports.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Presented the Finance Committee report on Customs Service audits, recommending it fix flagged problems and recover about MVR 2.2 million owed.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 21 to 24 (January 2025) declared accepted as no amendments were filed.
Ibrahim Didi (Kolamaafushi) named to the Judiciary Committee in place of Ismail Nizar (North Feydhoo).
Debate on the Maldives Civil Aviation Bill closed for the day, with no vote, to continue at a later sitting.
The Finance Committee report on the Customs Service audit reports for 2012 to 2019 passed 50-0.
Chair set the next sitting for Monday 12 May 2025 at 09:00 and noted the Majlis goes on break on 15 May.

votes.what: Passing the Finance Committee report on the Maldives Customs Service audit reports 2012 to 2019
